characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy aims to demonstrate that platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity solutions are technically viable in Denmark. It controls the scope and focus of the technical demonstrators, with the objective of providing credible evidence to support policy changes and procurement requirements. Key success metrics include the successful development of working demonstrators and their acceptance by relevant stakeholders as proof of concept.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy strongly supports the Procurement Influence Strategy by providing concrete examples of platform-neutral solutions. Demonstrators built under this lever can be directly referenced and showcased during procurement discussions, increasing the likelihood of adoption. It also supports Policy Advocacy Strategy by providing evidence.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: A highly ambitious Technical Feasibility Strategy could strain resources, potentially conflicting with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy if demonstrator development consumes too much budget. A narrow focus may also conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy if the chosen technology alienates some stakeholders.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy focuses on shaping the narrative around Denmark's digital identity infrastructure to emphasize resilience, continuity of service, and supplier concentration risks. It controls the messaging and arguments used to influence policymakers and the public. Success is measured by the inclusion of platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements in relevant policy documents and procurement specifications.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy works in synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy. A broader coalition, encompassing diverse perspectives, strengthens the advocacy position and increases the likelihood of influencing AltID requirements. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy by using concrete demonstrators as evidence.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Focusing too heavily on continuity of service might conflict with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy if it leads to Denmark advocating for solutions that are not aligned with broader European interoperability goals. It may also conflict with Procurement Influence Strategy if the policy asks are too broad.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy aims to create a broad base of support for platform-neutral digital identity in Denmark. It controls the scope and composition of the coalition, with the objective of amplifying advocacy efforts and increasing political pressure for change. Success is measured by the size and diversity of the coalition, as well as its ability to influence policy and procurement decisions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy amplifies the Policy Advocacy Strategy by providing a larger and more diverse platform for disseminating key messages. A strong coalition also enhances the Procurement Influence Strategy by demonstrating broad support for platform-neutral solutions. It also benefits from Technical Feasibility Strategy by having concrete examples to show.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Building a very broad coalition may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if diverse stakeholders demand support for a wide range of technical approaches, straining demonstrator development resources. It may also conflict with Procurement Influence Strategy if the coalition's goals are too diffuse.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy focuses on incorporating platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements into AltID and related digital identity procurement processes. It controls the specific language and criteria used in procurement documents, with the objective of incentivizing vendors to adopt supplier-neutral solutions. Success is measured by the inclusion of relevant requirements in official procurement documents.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy is directly supported by the Technical Feasibility Strategy, which provides concrete examples of platform-neutral solutions that vendors can implement. It also benefits from the Policy Advocacy Strategy, which creates a favorable political environment for including platform-neutral requirements. It also benefits from Coalition Building Strategy.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Advocating for very specific and stringent platform-neutral requirements may conflict with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy if those requirements are not aligned with broader European interoperability goals. It may also conflict with Technical Feasibility Strategy if the requirements are too difficult to implement.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy aims to align Danish advocacy for platform-neutral digital identity with broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, and resilience. It controls the project's engagement with relevant EU bodies and technical working groups. Success is measured by the project's contribution to relevant European Digital Identity Wallet materials.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy complements the Policy Advocacy Strategy by extending the project's influence beyond Denmark and aligning it with broader European trends. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy by showcasing Danish demonstrators as potential models for European standards. It also benefits from Coalition Building Strategy.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Actively championing a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU framework may conflict with the Procurement Influence Strategy if it leads to Denmark pursuing solutions that are incompatible with broader European standards. It may also conflict with Technical Feasibility Strategy if the sandbox requires too much effort.
